title: Localization-compatible affine charts for an arbitrary-open integral map
statement:
Let $S,U,V$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $j:U\hookrightarrow S$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $g:V	o U$ be an integral morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Assume that $f=j\circ g$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; it is separated, hence quasi-separated. Form the relative normalization $
u:N	o S$ of $S$ in $V$ [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization]. For every affine open $W\subseteq S$, put $A_W=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_S)$, $B_W=\Gamma(f^{-1}(W),\mathcal O_V)$ and $C_W$ equal to the integral closure of $A_W$ in $B_W$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], using the $A_W$-algebra structure induced by $f$. The canonical restriction diagram $W\mapsto C_W$ is compatible with localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]: for every principal affine restriction $D(a)\subseteq W$, its natural square with $A_W	o\Gamma(D(a),\mathcal O_S)$ is a pushout of commutative rings, equivalently $C_{D(a)}\cong(C_W)_a$ via the canonical restriction map. Thus its transition maps satisfy the cocycle condition and the affine schemes $\operatorname{Spec}(C_W)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] glue [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] to $N$. Explicitly, the canonical maps $\psi_W:\operatorname{Spec}(C_W)	o N$ are open immersions and jointly cover $N$, their images are exactly $
u^{-1}(W)$, and $
u\circ\psi_W$ is the spectrum of $A_W	o C_W$ followed by $\operatorname{Spec}(A_W)\cong W\hookrightarrow S$. The morphism $
u$ is integral and there is an isomorphism $e:N	imes_S U\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ over $U$ [def-pc-fibre-product], namely $g\circ e=\operatorname{pr}_U$.

source.place: Stacks Project, Morphisms Lemma 0CNX (lemma-extend-integral-surjective-morphisms), proof; Morphisms Lemmas 035F and 035K for localization-compatible charts

proof.text: The composite f=j∘g is separated because integral morphisms and open immersions are separated. With the explicitly assumed quasi-compactness, the relative normalization of S in V is defined as in Tag 035H. For each affine open W of S, its chart ring is C_W, the integral closure of Γ(W,O_S) in Γ(f⁻¹(W),O_V). These are full inverse-image sections, rather than separate rings over a cover of W∩U.

proof.text: Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of f ensure that f_*O_V is quasi-coherent. Its sections localize on principal affine restrictions. Apply integral-closure localization to obtain C_{D(a)}≅(C_W)_a, equivalently the canonical pushout square of base and closure rings. The restrictions form a functor; their compositions are the canonical transition maps and satisfy the triple-overlap cocycle law.

proof.text: The canonical relative gluing of Spec(C_W) along these principal restrictions gives the relative normalization N, with open chart maps ψ_W. They cover N and their images equal ν⁻¹(W); the chart maps to S are induced by A_W→C_W. Each full affine preimage ν⁻¹(W) is Spec(C_W), whose ring is integral over A_W, so ν is integral.

proof.text: By Tag 035K, relative normalization commutes with restriction to U. The pullback of f along the open immersion j is g, since j is a monomorphism. By Tag 03GP the normalization of the integral morphism g is V itself. Composing these canonical identifications gives e:N×_S U≅V, with e followed by g equal to the second projection.

statement_change.old_statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $j:U\hookrightarrow S$ be an arbitrary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $g:V\to U$ be an integral morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. For every affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subseteq S$, after refining $W\cap U$ by a principal affine open cover $W_i=D(f_i)$ with $V_i=g^{-1}(W_i)=\operatorname{Spec}(B_i)$, let $C_i$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $B_i$. The canonical localization identifications $(C_i)_{f_i f_j}\cong(C_j)_{f_i f_j}$ on every affine overlap are induced by localization of integral closure. They satisfy the cocycle condition, so the affine schemes $\operatorname{Spec}(C_i)$ glue compatibly as $W$ and the affine cover vary; the resulting glued scheme is integral over $S$ and restricts over $U$ to $V$.
statement_change.what: The proposed charts do not glue to an integral S-scheme, even with U=S, g=id, S=Spec(Q[t]). Take the principal cover D(t),D(1-t). Both C_i are Q[t], because Q[t] is integrally closed in Q(t). Gluing their spectra only along D(t(1-t)) doubles the points 0 and 1; the resulting map is not separated (hence not integral), and its restriction to U=S is not V=S. Also diagonal gluing overlaps must be the whole chart, not merely D(f_i²). The cited source defines relative normalization using sections on full inverse images of affine base opens and assumes its input quasi-compact and quasi-separated. An arbitrary open immersion need not make g≫j quasi-compact. Restore the required quasi-compactness and correct the chart rings and overlaps to the source construction; quasi-separatedness is automatic here. Tag 0CNX invokes normalization outside the hypotheses of its cited definition for an arbitrary open (and says “in U” where its recovery claim needs “in V”); it does not prove the invented principal-cover construction.

old_proof.text: Fix an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ of $S$ and a principal affine cover $W\cap U=\bigcup_iD(f_i)$, with $V_i=V\times_U D(f_i)=\operatorname{Spec}(B_i)$. Since $g$ is integral, the induced map $A_{f_i}\to B_i$ is integral. Regard $A\to B_i$ through $A\to A_{f_i}$ and define $C_i\subseteq B_i$ to be the integral closure of $A$ in $B_i$. This produces an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}(C_i)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, integral by the definition of integral closure and of an integral affine morphism.

source.place: Tag 0CNX proof, affine normalization charts; Morphisms Section 29.54

old_proof.text: On the overlap $D(f_if_j)$, the localization theorem for integral closure identifies $(C_i)_{f_if_j}$ with the integral closure of $A_{f_if_j}$ in $(B_i)_{f_if_j}$. Because $A_{f_i}\to B_i$ is integral, every element of $B_i$ is integral over $A_{f_i}$, so after localizing at $f_j$ this closure is $(B_i)_{f_j}$. The same calculation from the $j$-chart gives $(B_j)_{f_i}$, and the two are canonically identified with the restriction of $V$ to the common principal open. Localization is transitive, so these identifications agree on triple overlaps and obey the cocycle condition.

source.place: Morphisms Lemma 035K (normalization-localization), together with Tag 0307; more-morphisms.tex Tag 0CNX proof

old_proof.text: Apply the scheme-gluing theorem to the schemes $\operatorname{Spec}(C_i)$, their principal-open overlap subschemes, and the transition isomorphisms from Step 2. The identity, inverse, and triple-overlap equations just checked are precisely its gluing-data hypotheses. The glued scheme $V_W$ has open affine charts mapping to $W$; each chart ring $C_i$ is integral over $A$, hence $V_W\to W$ is integral, and its restriction over $W\cap U$ is identified with $V\times_U(W\cap U)$ by the localized chart identifications.

If $W'$ is another affine open of $S$, the constructions on $W$ and $W'$ restrict to the same charts on every affine principal refinement of $W\cap W'$, by the localization identifications of Step 2. The resulting chart isomorphisms satisfy the same cocycle condition, so the $V_W$ glue over an affine cover of $S$ to a scheme $V'\to S$. Integrality is affine-local on the target and therefore survives this gluing. On $U$ the localized charts are exactly the given $V_i$, so the base change $V'\times_SU$ is canonically isomorphic to $V$ over $U$.
